| **Assessed** | 2026-11-27 |

By 2040 a shrinking, ageing EU workforce meets an AI-driven jobs boom: AI automates routine tasks rather than displacing workers, competition for talent intensifies, and most workers and organisations benefit, supported by strong social dialogue and inclusive policy.

## Social contract scores (draft)

| Promise | Score | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Hard work pays | 4 | Automation lets affected workers upskill into higher-value roles in a tight labour market and disadvantaged groups gain from the search for talent, though career self-direction still depends on qualifications. |
| Affordable essentials |  | Not addressed: the extract says nothing on the cost of housing, food, energy or care. |
| Reliable safety net | 4 | Existing jobs are rarely destroyed and unions extend representation and protection to workers outside traditional contracts, though no income-support arrangements are described. |
| Responsive government | 4 | Tripartite social dialogue is strengthened, inclusiveness is a key factor in state decisions and sustainability becomes the core of most policy areas. |
| Time for what matters | 3 | Purpose-driven careers and voluntary job changes rise for some, but only 30% of respondents thought most workers would gain room for meaningful work, and screen-time concerns are flagged. |

## Policies from the atlas

- **Lifelong Learning Programs** (`lifelong-learning-programs`): Inclusiveness in education and training rises substantially as a policy priority, and micro-credentials become increasingly recognised as the education and training system becomes more flexible, accessible and responsive (pp. 30, 70, 90).
- **Union & Bargaining Rights** (`union-bargaining-rights`): Trade unions, employers' organisations and governments work together on technological change, and unions extend support to workers outside traditional contracts (p. 14).
